title: What is known about 1RB0RA_1LC1RA_0LD1LD_0LE0LC_1LA0LF_---1LC
description: Proof status of the six-state BB(6) holdout 1RB0RA_1LC1RA_0LD1LD_0LE0LC_1LA0LF_---1LC.
intro: Nobody knows whether this six-state, two-symbol Turing machine halts when started on a blank tape: it is one of the holdouts left open by the bbchallenge project. This page lists what has been established about it, sorted by what each result rests on.
verdict: The question is open. Lean proves, for every size and with any tape around them, the four moves of a unit (10)^x 00 (10)^y 110 0 1^w 0: its cycle with six blank cells to the left, its slower cycle against a wall of 1s, its turn into a wall when y is 0, and the return that makes a wall a unit again. What happens where two units meet is known only from simulation. An exact run-length simulator with phase jumps runs 5.1·1036 steps without a halt.

claims.title: The halting configurations
claims.text: The machine stops exactly when it reads the symbol of a halting transition (F0); the generated statement covers every configuration.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10,000 steps
claims.text: The list simulator of the shared library, proved to agree with the machine's semantics, runs 10,000 steps from blank tape without a halt, evaluated by Lean's kernel.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps
claims.text: The same run, evaluated by compiled code.

claims.title: The cycle and the phase at the left end
claims.text: P x y w R is A>0 (10)^x 00 (10)^y 110 0 1^w 0 R with blank tape to the left. One cycle: P x (y+1) w R reaches P (x+3) y (w+2) R in 8x + 4(y+1) + 26 steps, for every x, y, w and every tape R. A whole phase: P x y w R reaches P (x+3y) 0 (w+2y) R in pcost x y steps.

claims.title: The phase at any depth: six blank cells per cycle
claims.text: With U x y w = (10)^x 00 (10)^y 110 0 1^w 0: 0^(6k) A>0 U x (y+k) w reaches A>0 U (x+3k) y (w+2k) in k(8x+4y+16) + 14k2 steps, for every x, y, w, k, whatever is left of the 6k zeros and right of the unit.

claims.title: The phase against a wall of 1s: two 1s per cycle
claims.text: With the head on the last of 2k+2 ones, U (x+1) (y+k+1) w right of it: after (k+1)(8x+4y+24) + 6(k+1)2 steps the ones are gone, the unit is U (x+k+2) y (w+2k+2) and the head is on the cell that was left of the ones, whatever it holds.

claims.title: The turn and the return
claims.text: Turn: 0^9 A>0 U x 0 w R reaches, in 14x + 60 steps, a wall of 2x+10 ones with the head on the last of them, followed by 1 0 1^(w+4) 0 R. Return: 0^4 A>0 (10)^(x+1) 11 000 R reaches A>0 U 1 x 2 R in 4x + 16 steps. At the left end of the tape: a main phase P 1 y w R reaches the wall of 6y+12 ones, and A>0 (10)^(x+1) 11 000 R reaches the main phase P 1 x 2 R.

claims.title: From blank tape to the first three main phases
claims.text: Blank tape reaches P 1 4 2 R0 at step 173, P 1 14 2 R1 at step 1,225 and P 1 46 2 R2 at step 5,625 (R0, R1, R2 written out); each of these phases reaches its wall, of 36, 96 and 288 ones, at steps 735, 4,967 and 38,359.

claims.title: No halt in the first 5.1·10<sup>36</sup> steps
claims.text: c/macro.c keeps the tape as runs of 0, 1 and 10, crosses a run in one move and jumps over k cycles of a unit with the two phase rules proved in Lean. It runs 5,135,031,925,650,943,510,945,361,186,015,609,585 steps (37 main phases, 495 million moves, 8 seconds) without a halt; 64-bit counters stop it there. Tests: the whole tape equals the plain simulator's at 20 stops up to step 2,971,093; the main phase starts equal the plain simulator's up to 3.3·106 steps and agree with and without jumps up to 1015 steps (once, by hand, up to 1.3·1018).

claims.title: The main phases: y → 3y + 4, with an exception
claims.text: The phases at the left end that start with x = 1 have y = 4, 14, 46, 142, 430, …: from the second on y → 3y + 4, up to the 37th (y = 567,663,852,794,517,601, step 6.2·10<sup>35</sup>), except from the 17th (y = 229,582,510) to the 18th (y = 488,413,207 = 3y + 4 − 200,334,327). There the unit right of the wall went on against the wall with the slower cycle and took 200,334,327 pairs from it. So y → 3y + 4 is not a law of the machine.

claims.title: Where units meet
claims.text: How a unit is entered after a turn, how it freezes when its blank cells run out and when it goes on against the wall depend on a few cells at the joints. Classing every left turn of the head by the cell runs around it gives 387 classes in 1.5 million events up to 10<sup>28</sup> steps, the same 387 as up to 10<sup>20</sup>. They have not been written down as rules.

claims.title: Does it halt from blank tape?
claims.text: The only halting transition is F reading 0: a left sweep (C keeps a cell, D erases a 1, alternately) that finds 0 1 0 just left of a cell C passed, for example C arriving on the right end of (10)^2 1^m with m odd. Whether that can happen is a question about parities at the joints of the units, for which there is no macro machine yet.

check: python3 holdouts/1RB0RA_1LC1RA_0LD1LD_0LE0LC_1LA0LF_---1LC/py/test_macro.py  # macro.c against the plain simulator

explainer.lede: Nobody knows. The tape is a row of units, each a pair of counters and a block of 1s. A unit with blank cells to its left pours one counter into the other; when it is done it turns into a wall and hands its block of 1s to the next unit as blank cells, and the same happens there, level below level. Lean proves each of these moves for all sizes. The joints between units come in hundreds of small cases that nobody has written down, and the halting question hides there. No halt in 5.1·10<sup>36</sup> steps.

facts.text: One cycle of a unit, anywhere on the tape, using six blank cells; proved in Lean with the turn and the return.
No halt in the run-length simulator with phase jumps (8 seconds).
The 37 main phases so far; the 18th broke the pattern.

sections.heading: The shape of the run
html: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.501). Right of the start it stopped growing in the second half of the run (bounded so far, or growing so slowly that no record fell in the last half).
After 109 steps the tape spans 74,462 cells (55,464 left of the start, 19 right), with a density of 1s of 0.724.
These are measurements of one bounded run, sorted by tools/py/bbtools/triage.py; the macro structure behind them is the next thing to find.

sections.eyebrow: What the tape is made of
sections.heading: Units: two counters and a block of 1s
html: The tape is a row of units. A unit is (10)^x 00 (10)^y 110 0 1^w 0: a counter x written as x pairs 10, a counter y written the same way, and a block of w ones. Only one unit is running at any time; the others wait.

The running unit needs blank cells to its left. In one cycle (the head sweeps the unit twice) it moves one pair out of y, puts three pairs into x and two 1s into w, and grows six cells into the blank:

So with 6k blank cells it does k cycles: (x, y+k, w) → (x+3k, y, w+2k), in k(8x+4y+16) + 14k2 steps. The head never looks past the w-block and never further left than the six cells, which is why the rule holds anywhere on the tape. At the very left of the tape the blank is endless and the unit runs until y is 0.

sections.heading: Walls and gaps, level below level
html: A unit with y = 0 cannot cycle. It turns: its x pairs become a solid wall of 2x+10 ones, and the head erases the w-block on its way right. Those erased cells, about w of them, are now blank cells in front of the next unit, which starts to run its own phase in them. If that unit reaches y = 0 before its gap is used up, it turns too, and the unit after it runs. The tape becomes a stack: wall, gap, wall, gap, …, running unit.

When a gap is used up the running unit freezes where it is and the head walks back to the wall on its left. The wall turns back into pairs and becomes a unit again: (10)^(x+1) 11 000 becomes the unit with x = 1, y = x and w = 2 (the return). So what a unit collected in x during one phase is what it has to pour during the next. That unit then runs on in whatever is left of its own gap.

There is one more move: a unit that has 1s to its left instead of blank cells (the wall itself) runs a slower cycle that takes two 1s from the wall and gives itself one pair: (x, y+1, w) → (x+1, y, w+2). A unit can eat into the wall of the level above it this way.
An example from the run, between the second and third main phase (T^n stands for (10)^n; each line is a moment when the head turns at the left of the running unit):

sections.heading: Main phases: y → 3y + 4, until it is not
html: At the left end of the tape the phase always completes. A main phase starts as the unit (1, y, w), ends as (3y+1, 0, w+2y), turns into a wall of 6y+12 ones, and the head goes off to the right. If the wall is untouched when the head comes back, the return makes it the unit (1, 3y+4, 2): the next main phase.

A main phase takes about 14y2 steps, so each is about nine times as long as the one before. For sixteen phases in a row y → 3y + 4. Then, on the trip after the 17th, the unit right of the wall went on against the wall with the slower cycle 200,334,327 times, and the 18th main phase started with 200,334,327 pairs fewer. After that the pattern holds again up to the 37th phase, as far as the simulator goes. Nothing says when it breaks next: the levels below feed back into the top one.

sections.heading: Where units meet
html: The four moves above are exact and proved. What is missing is what happens at the joints: how the head enters a unit after a turn, in which half of its cycle a unit freezes when fewer than six blank cells are left, and when it goes on against the wall instead. These depend on a few cells: how much of the gap is left (0 to 5 cells), whether w is 2 or 3, whether x is 0.

Sorting every left turn of the head by the runs of cells around it (with every long run counted as “long”) gives 387 different pictures in 1.5 million turns up to 1028 steps, and the same 387 already at 1020. So the machine very likely is a finite set of rules on the list of units, but nobody has written them down, and without them there is no way to argue about all of the run at once.

sections.heading: Where it could halt
html: The only missing transition is F reading 0. F is entered only from E reading 1, and E only from D reading 0. Going left, C and D alternate: C leaves its cell alone, D turns a 1 into a 0. The machine halts when such a sweep finds 0 1 0 just left of a cell C passed. For example, C arriving at the right end of 10 10 1^m halts when m is odd and passes when m is even.
So halting is a matter of parity at the joints of the units. In 5.1·1036 steps the parity was always right. A proof would need the rules of the joints and an invariant that keeps it right.

sections.heading: What is proved
html: Lean (kernel): the cycle with six blank cells, the cycle against a wall of 1s, k cycles of either at once with the exact step count, the turn and the return, each for every size and every tape around it (lean/Gap.lean, lean/Levels.lean); the cycle and phase at the left end (lean/Rules.lean, lean/Phase.lean). Lean (native_decide): blank tape reaches the first three main phases (steps 173, 1,225, 5,625) and each reaches its wall (lean/Reach.lean); no halt in 107 steps (lean/Blank.lean). Computed: no halt in 5.1·1036 steps (c/macro.c, tested against the plain simulator). Heuristic: the main phase table, the account of the 18th phase, the 387 kinds of joint. Open: the rules of the joints and the halting question.

family: nested two-counter units (walls and gaps), chaotic fractal
summary: The tape is a row of units (10)^x 00 (10)^y 110 0 1^w; a unit with blank cells to its left moves y into x three pairs at a time, then turns into a wall of 1s and hands its w-block to the next unit as blank cells, and so on down the tape (cycle, phase, turn and return proved in Lean for all sizes); the joints between units are not described; no halt in 5.1e36 steps; open.
